I can't speak for the whole of the country, but here in Ontario there's already sort of a "sugar tax". Foods that are deemed "essential" (like veggies and meats) don't have HST (Harmonized Sales Tax). For things like soda, candy, and chips, you have to pay HST on top of the price. Right now HST is 13% in the province, so you'd pay an extra 13% on top of the price for any "non-essential" food items.

I would be in favour of adding an additional tax on top of that though, sort of the way alcohol is taxed in the province. Say you buy a bottle of vodka - firstly, it's marked up already because the government has a monopoly - then you're paying 13% HST and I think another 6% as a liquor tax, though I could be wrong on that last value. A lot of people would be upset with a sugar tax because, "I only eat these things as a treat! Why should I have to pay because someone else abuses these substances?" But it's the same thing with liquor - I'm only a casual drinker, but I still pay the tax to offset the cost of healthcare for the alcoholics.
